column1: The nineteenth century was a period of great technological development in Britain, and for shipping the major changes were from wind to steam power, and from wood to iron and steel.
column2: 19世纪，英国技术突飞猛进。在航运业，最大的变化是动力由风力转向蒸汽，造船材料由木材转向铁和钢。

column1: The fastest commercial sailing vessels of all time were clippers, three-masted ships built to transport goods around the world, although some also took passengers.
column2: 史上最快的商用帆船是飞剪船。这种三桅船建造之初用于向世界各地运货，也有些搭载乘客。

column1: From the 1840s until 1869, when the Suez Canal opened and steam propulsion was replacing sail, clippers dominated world trade.
column2: 从19世纪40年代直到1869年苏伊士运河开通、蒸汽推进开始取代风帆之时，飞剪船一直主宰着世界贸易。

column1: Although many were built, only one has survived more or less intact: Cutty Sark, now on display in Greenwich, southeast London.
column2: 当年建成的飞剪船很多，只有卡蒂萨克号大致完整地留存至今，如今在伦敦东南部的格林尼治展出。

column1: Cutty Sark’s unusual name comes from the poem Tam O’Shanter by the Scottish poet Robert Burns.
column2: 卡蒂萨克号的船名颇为特别，出自苏格兰诗人罗伯特·彭斯的诗作《塔姆·奥尚特》。

column1: Tam, a farmer, is chased by a witch called Nannie, who is wearing a ‘cutty sark’ — an old Scottish name for a short nightdress.
column2: 诗中，农夫塔姆被一个名叫南妮的女巫追赶。女巫身穿一件“cutty sark”，是苏格兰人从前对短睡衣的叫法。

column1: The witch is depicted in Cutty Sark’s figurehead — the carving of a woman typically at the front of old sailing ships.
column2: 卡蒂萨克号的船首像刻的就是这名女巫。旧时帆船的船首通常有一尊这样的女性雕像。

column1: In legend, and in Burns’s poem, witches cannot cross water, so this was a rather strange choice of name for a ship.
column2: 传说中的女巫不能过水，彭斯的诗里也是如此，因此选这个名字来给船命名颇为奇怪。

column1: Cutty Sark was built in Dumbarton, Scotland, in 1869, for a shipping company owned by John Willis.
column2: 1869年，卡蒂萨克号在苏格兰的邓巴顿建成，订造这条船的是约翰·威利斯拥有的一家航运公司。

column1: To carry out construction, Willis chose a new shipbuilding firm, Scott & Linton, and ensured that the contract with them put him in a very strong position.
column2: 威利斯选了新成立的造船公司斯科特与林顿来承建，并确保签下的合同让自己处于十分有利的地位。
column7: in a very strong position|处于十分有利的地位

column1: In the end, the firm was forced out of business, and the ship was finished by a competitor.
column2: 最终，这家公司被迫停业，船由一家竞争对手接手完工。
column4: forced out of business|被迫停业

column1: Willis’s company was active in the tea trade between China and Britain, where speed could bring shipowners both profits and prestige, so Cutty Sark was designed to make the journey more quickly than any other ship.
column2: 威利斯的公司活跃于中英茶叶贸易，在这个行业，速度既能为船东带来利润，又能带来声望，因此，卡蒂萨克号的设计目标是比其他任何船都更快地跑完这条航线。
column9: make the journey|走完这段航程

column1: On her maiden voyage, in 1870, she set sail from London, carrying large amounts of goods to China.
column2: 1870年首航时，卡蒂萨克号载着大量货物，由伦敦启航前往中国。

column1: She returned laden with tea, making the journey back to London in four months.
column2: 返程时，船上满载茶叶，用了四个月驶回伦敦。
column4: making the journey back|走完返程

column1: However, Cutty Sark never lived up to the high expectations of her owner, as a result of bad winds and various misfortunes.
column2: 然而，由于风向不利，又屡遭不幸，卡蒂萨克号始终没能达到船主的厚望。

column1: On one occasion, in 1872, the ship and a rival clipper, Thermopylae, left port in China on the same day.
column2: 1872年有一次，卡蒂萨克号与竞争对手温泉关号飞剪船在同一天从中国港口出发。
column4: rival clipper|作为对手的飞剪船
column6: on the same day|在同一天

column1: Crossing the Indian Ocean, Cutty Sark gained a lead of over 400 miles, but then her rudder was severely damaged in stormy seas, making her impossible to steer.
column2: 横渡印度洋时，卡蒂萨克号一度领先400多英里；但在狂风巨浪中，船舵严重受损，船因而无法操纵。
column4: gained a lead of|取得……的领先优势

column1: The ship’s crew had the daunting task of repairing the rudder at sea, and only succeeded at the second attempt.
column2: 船员不得不在海上修舵，这项任务十分艰巨。他们直到第二次尝试才告成功。
column7: at the second attempt|在第二次尝试时

column1: Cutty Sark reached London a week after Thermopylae.
column2: 卡蒂萨克号比温泉关号晚了一周才抵达伦敦。

column1: Steam ships posed a growing threat to clippers, as their speed and cargo capacity increased.
column2: 随着航速和载货能力提高，蒸汽船对飞剪船构成的威胁越来越大。
column4: posed a growing threat to|对……构成日益加剧的威胁

column1: In addition, the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869, the same year that Cutty Sark was launched, had a serious impact.
column2: 此外，苏伊士运河的开通也带来重大影响。那是1869年，恰好也是卡蒂萨克号下水的年份。
column7: had a serious impact|产生了重大影响

column1: While steam ships could make use of the quick, direct route between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the canal was of no use to sailing ships, which needed the much stronger winds of the oceans, and so had to sail a far greater distance.
column2: 蒸汽船能利用这条连接地中海和红海的快捷直达航线，帆船却用不上运河。它们需要大洋上强劲得多的风，因此必须航行远得多的距离。
column7: was of no use to|对……无用
column9: far greater distance|远得多的距离

column1: Steam ships reduced the journey time between Britain and China by approximately two months.
column2: 蒸汽船把英国与中国之间的航程缩短了约两个月。
column5: by approximately two months|缩短了约两个月

column1: By 1878, tea traders weren’t interested in Cutty Sark, and instead, she took on the much less prestigious work of carrying any cargo between any two ports in the world.
column2: 到了1878年，茶商已对卡蒂萨克号失去兴趣。它只好接下声望低得多的运输活计，世界上哪两座港口之间有货可运，它就运什么。

column1: In 1880, violence aboard the ship led ultimately to the replacement of the captain with an incompetent drunkard who stole the crew’s wages.
column2: 1880年，船上发生暴力事件，最终导致船长被替换。接任的是个无能的酒鬼，还偷走了船员的工资。

column1: He was suspended from service, and a new captain appointed.
column2: 他被停职，随后任命了新船长。

column1: This marked a turnaround and the beginning of the most successful period in Cutty Sark’s working life, transporting wool from Australia to Britain.
column2: 这成了转机。卡蒂萨克号从澳大利亚向英国运送羊毛，从而开始了它服役生涯中最为成功的一段时期。

column1: One such journey took just under 12 weeks, beating every other ship sailing that year by around a month.
column2: 其中一次航行只用了不到12周，比当年跑这条航线的其他任何一条船都快了约一个月。
column5: every other ship|其他每一条船
column6: by around a month|快了约一个月

column1: The ship’s next captain, Richard Woodget, was an excellent navigator, who got the best out of both his ship and his crew.
column2: 下一任船长理查德·伍德盖特是一位出色的航海家，既能充分发挥船的性能，也能让船员展现最好的本领。
column4: got the best out of|使……发挥最大效能
column5: both his ship and his crew|船与船员两者

column1: As a sailing ship, Cutty Sark depended on the strong trade winds of the southern hemisphere, and Woodget took her further south than any previous captain, bringing her dangerously close to icebergs off the southern tip of South America.
column2: 作为一艘帆船，卡蒂萨克号依靠南半球强劲的信风航行。伍德盖特把船驶到了比历任船长都更靠南的海域，危险地逼近了南美洲南端海面上的冰山。

column1: His gamble paid off, though, and the ship was the fastest vessel in the wool trade for ten years.
column2: 不过，他这场冒险有了回报。有十年之久，这艘船一直是羊毛贸易中速度最快的船。

column1: As competition from steam ships increased in the 1890s, and Cutty Sark approached the end of her life expectancy, she became less profitable.
column2: 19世纪90年代，蒸汽船带来的竞争越发激烈，卡蒂萨克号也接近预期使用寿命的终点，其盈利能力随之下降。

column1: She was sold to a Portuguese firm, which renamed her Ferreira.
column2: 船被卖给一家葡萄牙公司，并被改名为费雷拉号。

column1: For the next 25 years, she again carried miscellaneous cargoes around the world.
column2: 接下来的25年，它再次环游世界，运送各种杂货。
column3: For the next 25 years|在随后的25年里

column1: Badly damaged in a gale in 1922, she was put into Falmouth harbour in southwest England, for repairs.
column2: 1922年，这艘船在大风中严重损坏，因而驶入英格兰西南部的法尔茅斯港维修。

column1: Wilfred Dowman, a retired sea captain who owned a training vessel, recognised her and tried to buy her, but without success.
column2: 威尔弗雷德·道曼是一位退休船长，拥有一艘训练船。他认出了这艘船，试图将它买下，却未能如愿。

column1: She returned to Portugal and was sold to another Portuguese company.
column2: 船返回葡萄牙，被卖给了当地另一家公司。

column1: Dowman was determined, however, and offered a high price: this was accepted, and the ship returned to Falmouth the following year and had her original name restored.
column2: 但道曼仍未放弃，报出了高价。这一次，对方接受了；船在次年回到法尔茅斯，并恢复了原名。
column4: offered a high price|开出高价
column7: had her original name restored|恢复了原来的船名

column1: Dowman used Cutty Sark as a training ship, and she continued in this role after his death.
column2: 道曼把卡蒂萨克号用作训练船，他去世后，这艘船依然承担着同样的任务。
column3: used Cutty Sark as|把卡蒂萨克号用作
column5: continued in this role|继续承担这一任务

column1: When she was no longer required, in 1954, she was transferred to dry dock at Greenwich to go on public display.
column2: 到了1954年，人们已不再需要它担任训练船，于是将它转移到格林尼治的干船坞，向公众展出。
column6: go on public display|开始向公众展出

column1: The ship suffered from fire in 2007, and again, less seriously, in 2014, but now Cutty Sark attracts a quarter of a million visitors a year.
column2: 这艘船在2007年经历火灾，2014年再次失火，后一次受损较轻。如今，卡蒂萨克号每年吸引25万名游客。
column6: a quarter of a million|二十五万
